Rep. Roger Williams highlights Texas economic growth and reflects on government shutdown
Rep. Roger Williams shared updates on economic initiatives like the Port Alpha shipyard and reflected on last year's government shutdown via social media posts dated September 30 and October 1, 2026
Rep. Roger Williams, a member of the U.S. House of Representatives from Texas, recently shared updates on economic development and political events in Texas through his social media posts.
On September 30, 2026, Williams highlighted the groundbreaking of a major shipbuilding project: "Texas is building the future of American shipbuilding. Today, Saronic broke ground on its $3.2 billion Port Alpha shipyard in Brownsville, Texas. This will be the largest shipyard in the country, creating up to 10,000 jobs and generating an estimated $264.5 billion in" (September 30, 2026).
The following day, Williams addressed the anniversary of a significant federal government shutdown, "One year ago today, Democrats shut down the federal government for 42 days. As @HouseGOP acted to reopen the government, Democrats voted time and again to block those efforts. The result was one of the longest government shutdowns in U.S. history. A failed political protest" (October 1, 2026).
Williams also described participating in an official visit with President Biden and other members of Congress: "This morning, it was a great honor to join @POTUS and some of my fellow Texans in Congress aboard Air Force One en route to Peterbilt Motors’ manufacturing facility in Denton, Texas." (October 1, 2026).
Roger Williams has maintained his seat in Congress through multiple election cycles since first winning office in 2012. He secured victories against opponents such as Elaine M. Henderson (2012), Marco Montoya (2014), Kathi Thomas (2016), Julie Oliver (2018 and 2020), and Chad Hagg (2024). In his most recent race in 2024, he won by a substantial margin.
